request.abstract: a cascaded array of 56 programmable Mach–Zehnder interferometers in a silicon photonic integrated circuit and show its utility for vowel recognition.

transcript.text: Who would you talk to about the work, and what slows them down?
I'd start with AI infrastructure teams at data center operators. Inference loads are growing, and their existing accelerators can run up against a rack's power budget.
What did the paper demonstrate, and what would you test with a buyer?

We demonstrated a programmable silicon photonic circuit on a vowel recognition task. It was a research prototype. In a pilot, we'd measure energy per inference and accuracy on the buyer's own workload. We're exploring an optical inference accelerator for teams that need to stay within a rack's power budget.
Who owns that evaluation, and when would they look at it?

The head of AI infrastructure would sponsor the evaluation, with the data center engineering lead checking power and integration. I'd talk to them when they're planning the next accelerator refresh and the existing rack power budget limits what they can add.
